To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the light output and time resolution of a scintillator rod degrade exponentially from one end, and that the inverse slopes are twice as large for the timing characteristics as for the light output.

(1) the timing degradation of a long scintillator rod is due to the photoelectron statistics of the light signal, and (2) this degradation is exponential with a characteristic decay distance of 0.5 m for our scintillators.

the time resolution of a long thin scintillator is proportional to the inverse of the number of photoelectrons, and that the number of photo-electrons decreases exponentially along the length of the scintillator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel type of plastic scintillator, which is suitable for the construction of a time-of-flight (TOF) counter for the relativistic heavy ion experiment at the BNL AGS.
the study of timing degradation in long plastic scinitillator rods for time-of- flight counters in relativistic ion experiments.
the design, fabrication, and testing of plastic scintillators for the time of flight (TOF) system of the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron (AGS) at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the light attenuation is the dominant cause of timing degradation.

the light yield and time resolution of a long scintillator rod are both exponential functions of the distance from one of the ends, with the inverse slope parameters of the time resolution twice that of the light yield.
the timing resolution of long plastic scintillator counters can be improved by increasing the light output, which can be achieved by increasing the thickness and/or length of the scintillator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time resolution is dominated by the light yield and that the time resolution of long scintillators is not limited by the scintillation lifetime but by the light attenuation.
the light yield is the most important parameter in determining the time resolution, and the light yield degradation is the dominant effect in the time resolution degradation.
the light attenuation and the timing degradation are not the same in long plastic scinitillators, and the timing degradation can be described by a simple model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the timing resolution of a scintillator counter can be significantly improved by placing a photomultiplier tube at each end of the counter.

a large fraction of the scintillation light must reach both ends of the scintillator for the best timing performance, which is a key consideration for the design and operation of time-of-flight counters.
a scintillator rod should be used in such a way that the distance to be measured is not longer than 1/2 the inverse slope parameters.
